corrections.claim: BLOCKING, 11_chat_scroll.mp4: the framework's build spikes to 916-1462 ms on 26 of 642 frames at a period of exactly 25 frames, so 'the year-deep thread stops for over a second to rebuild roughly every 0.4 s of scrolling'.
corrections.what_i_measured: The numbers reproduce exactly: 26 entries over 500 ms, gaps 23-27, 916-1462 ms, median 1197, 31,674 of 36,583 ms = 86.6 per cent of all build time, and the distribution is bimodal with nothing at all between 90 ms and 916 ms. The frequency and the cause do not. per_frame is framework frames, not driven steps: 642 frames over 300 grabs, 2.14 per step, so 25 entries is 11.7 steps = 187 ms of app time, not 400. And the spacing is constant in time, not in scrolling: 5.1-6.4 s of framework-accounted time between spikes (mean 5.9) and 531,790/26 = 20,453 ms of wall clock, while the thread's travel per frame falls from 143 to 31 device px across the same clip without the spacing changing. 20.4 s is app/lib/transport/sync.dart:140, `once(wait: const Duration(seconds: 20))`. The frames step took 531.8 s of wall clock to drive 4.8 s of app time, a ratio of 111:1, so anything periodic on the wall clock is oversampled about a hundredfold against app time. A 1.2 s build is still a 1.2 s build and worth a finding; it is a sync round costing it, once every twenty seconds of real time, not the thread rebuilding every 0.4 s of a scroll.

corrections.claim: BLOCKING, 06_unfolding.mp4: the unfolding sheet is a machine-cut rectangle — left edge a single column over 90 rows (std 0.00 px), top exactly 1074 and bottom exactly 1503 at frame 325 — while neighbours wander 22-35 px; and the fold is 'a flat image being transformed'.
corrections.what_i_measured: The shape claim stands and is if anything understated: at frame 325 the top edge holds std 0.43 px and the bottom std 0.00 px over 701 columns, while the sheet directly below it has a top edge of std 15.9 px and 107 px peak-to-peak. At frame 46 the left edge is std 0.53 over 90 rows (not 0.00) and 0.09 over the 110 rows below the crease. The mechanism is wrong. This is not a flat image being transformed: assets/folds/unfold_thirds/0046.png is a Cycles render whose opaque left edge sits in column 61 for all 209 rows (std 0.00) and right edge in column 538 (std 0.00), and blender/folds/fold.py models a sheet at real size with bevelled crease geometry and a shadow catcher in the same frame. The sheet is straight because the model is a machine-cut rectangle, which is a worse fault to name and a different one to fix.

corrections.claim: BLOCKING, 06_unfolding.mp4 frame 46: the fold is a one-dimensional gradient — median per-row standard deviation across the 580-px width 1.50 grey, the vertical profile the same to within 2 grey at five x positions, and the crease a 20.5-grey step in one pixel row at y=1429.
corrections.what_i_measured: Median per-row standard deviation across x 120-700, y 1350-1560: 1.48. The five profiles do run together — plateau ~180, trough ~111-117, second plateau ~158-166, step to ~236 — but the median spread across x=100/200/400/600/700 at a given row is 5.0 grey, not 2. The crease is not a one-pixel step: at x=400 it falls 163 to 111 over six rows (y 1424-1430); the steepest single row is 19 grey. The load-bearing number reproduces; the crease sentence is the steepest row of a six-row ramp described as the whole thing.

corrections.claim: BLOCKING, 06_unfolding.mp4: the cast shadow is a hard slab — 247.8 to 108.0 to 30.0 across four rows then flat at 30-37 for 60 px.
corrections.what_i_measured: Reproduces. At frame 325, x=400 the luma runs 248, 224, 186, 108, 46, 30 over five rows and then holds between 30 and 40 for about 70 px before rising. And the slab is in the asset, not applied afterwards: the packed fold frame's own alpha steps 255 to 182 in two rows and holds 158-182 for 46 rows before falling off over eight. It is a shadow-catcher bake that came out flat.

corrections.claim: BLOCKING, 06_unfolding.mp4: the unfolding sheet carries 0.90 grey levels of micro-texture against 4.56 on the settled note beside it, a 5.1x deficit — 'the paper only acquires tooth after it lands'.
corrections.what_i_measured: The ratio reproduces at frame 46: 4.49 on the roster note against 0.77 on the fold sheet's upper face and 1.11 on its front panel, 4.0 to 5.8x. The explanation is wrong twice over. It does not acquire tooth after it lands: the same sheet at rest measures 1.88 at frame 162 and 1.47 at frame 325, against 4.20-4.36 for the notes around it in those same frames. And the tooth is not missing from the source — assets/folds/unfold_thirds/0046.png carries 9.28 grey levels of it, the packed WebP is lossless and carries the identical 9.28, and 6.11 survives upscaling to the on-screen 712 px. So the loss is between the asset and the glass. The gap between 0.77 while moving and 1.88 at rest is the clip's own libx264 -crf 16 encode smoothing a moving region, which is an artifact of how the evidence was made; the residual 2.4x deficit at rest is the build's and is the finding worth keeping.

corrections.claim: SERIOUS, 02_chat.png: the bottom sheet is sliced by a straight cut with no shadow — a 138.4-grey step in one un-antialiased row, the desk 2-5 px beneath reading 94.64 against 94.61 twelve pixels away.

corrections.claim: BLOCKING, 08_state_propagating.mp4: no partner-state change is ever visible happening — the clip reads TRAVELLING at frame 394 and OUT at frame 395 across a splice.

corrections.claim: WHAT IS WORKING: the receiving page's displacement reproduces the feeling's waveform — 'hold' holds 56 frames, dips six at 912-992 ms, holds again and stops at 1888 ms against 1900; 'here' gives three 25-frame lifts and two settles ending at index 124 = 1984 ms against 2000; a plain message moves the page zero pixels across all nineteen frames of its run; peak displacement about 0.12 device px per amplitude unit.

not_looked_at: 17_setup_pwa.png — the only one of the fifteen present artifacts nobody read. It appears three times in six reports and every one is about its file identity (anti-goal: 'shot on the same headless WebKit'; coherence: byte-identical header band, and a DIFF judgement). Nobody read what is on it. What is on it: 'this one, the iphone', 'add it to the home screen — share, then add to home screen. it will not hold on to anything until you do', 'put this phone on the tailnet', 'install the profile the other phone is serving — open its address in Safari, take the profile, then trust it in settings under about, certificate trust settings', 'read the six words off the other phone'.

evidence/crops/dusk_pulse.png with logs/dusk_pulse.json and .report.json — a full 1440x3120 capture of Pulse at light: dusk, its own scene file, its own report (14,062 events, six feeling receipts, twelve partner-state facts). Not one of the seventeen, not a derived measurement, and opened by nobody. It is the only evidence in the set for the second lighting state the build ships, and it bears directly on the material row's 'one consistent light direction' and the coherence row's 'one visual language'.

evidence/crops/02_chat_300_shadow.png — the third of the three 300 per cent crops logs/crops.json names. The material critic judged the hand crop and the edge crop and said both land in the wrong place; the shadow crop, which is the one that would have tested its own contact-shadow findings at 300 per cent, went unopened.

evidence/crops/haptics_strip.png — the picture of the haptic vocabulary. The emotional critic judged all thirty-six patterns from the millisecond table in haptics.json and wrote 'a table of milliseconds is not a demonstration' without opening the strip that logs/haptics.check.json points at.
evidence/crops/reception_open.png and reception_allowed.png — two of the four reception crops. Only reception.png (anti-goal) and reception_replaced.png (emotional) were used.

evidence/logs/hand.json — named in the briefing as one of the four logs a critic can check against the pictures, and cited by nobody. It reports 516 ink marks on 02_chat with 86 near-twins, a 16.7 per cent twin share at IoU 0.85. The material critic did its own version of this measurement (158 marks, 8.9 per cent at correlation 0.99) and never set it against the log; the two disagree by 3.3x on the mark count and by nearly 2x on the twin share, and nothing in the cycle reconciles them.

evidence/logs/webpush.txt — nobody read it. It is the only evidence that the push path is real crypto (RFC 8291 record matches, round trip recovers the plaintext, the payload carries only kind and from, VAPID ES256 JWT in three parts). It bears on both the emotional row's closed-app clause and the code row's rules 6 and 7.

evidence/logs/strings.json (13 KB), logs/recipes.json (129 recipes, 501 objects), logs/manifest.json — uncited. manifest.json records two manifest entries with no file (fonts/MANIFEST.fonts.json, tears/tears.json); the code critic checked only the other direction, files without an entry, and found none.
evidence/logs/pwa.json's display_mode_standalone: false — the anti-goal critic used this file for its icon list and nobody read the line that says the served page was not running as an installed app.
The four missing-platform gaps were taken and taken well: 09_two_devices.png and 16_setup_android.png are named as absent by five of the six reports, and the webkit-only capture by four.
gaps: Two reports read 08_state_propagating in opposite directions and neither could see the other: coherence lists 'state reaches a region that is not Pulse, in motion' among the things working, while emotional makes the same clip's state changes its first blocking finding. The scene script settles it against coherence. Nothing in a six-critic fan-out reconciles two readings of one artifact, and this cycle has no mechanism that would have caught it.

The iOS install flow is pictured and unexamined. 17_setup_pwa.png tells the reader to install and trust a certificate profile in iOS Settings under About, Certificate Trust Settings, and that the app 'will not hold on to anything until you do' add it to the home screen. A CA-trust step and a lose-your-data-until-installed step in the onboarding of half the mission, on the glass, judged by nobody. The anti-goal critic explicitly declined to certify onboarding voice because 16_setup_android is missing, while the PWA half of the onboarding was sitting in the evidence directory.

Nothing in the evidence shows the app running as an installed home-screen web app, and logs/pwa.json's own display_mode_standalone: false says the one PWA measurement was taken in a tab. logs/reception.json says iOS gives the push API only to a home-screen web app. So the installable-PWA half of the mission has no artifact behind it in the state that matters, and no report says so in those words.

The dusk lighting state was judged by nobody, so 'one consistent light direction' and 'one visual language across all five regions' were both decided on one of the two lighting states the build ships.

The sound in the clips is not the app's output — logs/07_feeling_landing.sound.json and 15_authored_feeling.sound.json both say the feeling's ogg was mixed over silence at the arrival frame. The emotional critic noted the file lengths; no rubric row asks whether the app's own audio output works, and no evidence shows it.

What the evidence does not show at all, beyond the two absent stills: any Android pixel; the vibrator firing; two devices in one frame; the first launch (13.2-13.7 s cold against 2.75-3.36 s warm, on the glass nowhere); the queued 'waiting to send' state; the feeling-authoring drawer, where the anti-goal critic found a gold star and a crown still reachable; a media search returning media; and Moments in two of its three lenses (183 of 1,677 events).

No rubric row visibly covers onboarding as a capability, accessibility or text scaling, or what the glass shows while the tailnet is down — the last of which is the state the whole transport argument is about.

The tree moved under the review. DIFF.json names commit 4dd3537; HEAD is 4eeea98; app/lib/regions/chat/search_page.dart, viewer_page.dart and app/lib/material/slip.dart all carry mtimes after 07:51, when the last of the six reports was written, and the search and viewer files now contain fixes for exactly the two blocking findings against them, one of them quoting the finding in a comment. A cycle that judges an evidence set thirteen-fifteenths of which predates its own capture has the same problem one level up: two of the cycle's seven blocking findings are already answered in code no report read.

evidence/reliability.json and evidence/coldstart.json regenerated while this pass was running (08:05 to 08:20). The capability matrix came back identical — 174 events both sides, no duplicates, seq 1..173 gapless, 26 queued offline — so the messenger critic's reading of it is reproducible on demand. The tailnet later_check is still 'pending ... the nodes were not answering', so the reservations both messenger and coherence put on the three-day-old tailnet run are current rather than stale.

Nobody counted the reports. 14_media_viewer.report.json reads 14,073 events where coherence's one-log claim says every per-region report reads 14,062, and 10_first_run and 17_setup_pwa read 0. The counts are the cheapest cross-check in the evidence and only one report used them, without checking them.
verdict: The review is in better shape than the build it reviewed. I reproduced every blocking finding in the six reports and all but one of the headline numbers, and most came out within a per cent or two of what was claimed: the search screen's 67 per cent chrome, the media viewer's three elements, the fold sheet's 0.00-px edges against a neighbour's 107 px of wander, its shadow slab holding flat for seventy pixels, its 4.5-against-1 texture deficit, the state change landing across a splice, the haptic waveform inverted to the millisecond (23,275 ms of buzz becoming 16,860 ms of silence), the Flutter logo's md5, the scroll tracking its own fling log to two tenths of a device pixel, and the whole of the emotional row's central measurement — three lifts and two settles for 'here' ending at 1984 ms against a declared 2000, and nineteen frames of exactly zero for a plain message. That last is the strongest thing in the cycle and it survived every way I tried to break it. Four claims did not survive. The scroll's build spikes are real but they are not a scrolling cost: per_frame counts framework frames, not driven steps, and the spikes are spaced 20.4 seconds apart on the wall clock, which is app/lib/transport/sync.dart's twenty-second long poll, oversampled a hundredfold because the harness spent 531 seconds of wall clock driving 4.8 seconds of app time — that is a finding about how the evidence was made wearing the clothes of a finding about the thread. The fold sheet's missing tooth is real at rest (1.5-1.9 against 4.2-4.4) but the 5.1x figure is measured at the worst frame of a moving region under libx264, and 'the paper only acquires tooth after it lands' is the opposite of what happens; the straight edges and the flat shadow are in the Blender asset itself, so the material critic's 'a flat image being transformed' names the wrong mechanism for a fault that is worse than the one it names. And coherence's 'state reaches a region that is not Pulse, in motion' is simply wrong — the scene script pushes both state lines between capture runs — which means two of the six reports read the same clip in opposite directions and the cycle had no way to notice. What the review did not do is look. Fifteen artifacts were present and fourteen were read; 17_setup_pwa.png was not, and it is the screen that tells a reader to install and trust a certificate profile on their iPhone and warns that the app keeps nothing until it is on the home screen — the largest unexamined fact about half the mission. crops/dusk_pulse.png, a full-resolution capture of the whole material system under its second light, was opened by nobody. logs/hand.json, which the briefing names as one of four checkable logs, was cited by nobody and reports a 16.7 per cent twin share where the one critic who measured the hand reported 8.9. And the cycle's own conclusions have already gone stale: two of its blocking findings are answered in files modified after the last report was filed.
